claims.claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs were entirely lacking Nkx2.2, Isl1/2 and Olig2 expression and instead expressed Pax7.
claims.source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs were entirely lacking Nkx2.2, Isl1/2 and Olig2 expression and instead expressed Pax7, as did Smo-/- nEBs (Figure 1C,F,I,L,O,R).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: All Smoothened-/- nEBs acquired highly dorsal fates as cells refractory to Shh pathway activation.
claims.source: All Smo-/- nEBs thus conformed to the standard signaling model by acquiring highly dorsal fates as cells refractory to Shh pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the data showing Pax7 expression in Smo-/- nEBs.

claims.claim: Each clone had abundant Pax6+ nuclei and Tuj1 expression, suggesting robust neuralization.
claims.source: Each clone had abundant Pax6+ nuclei and Tuj1 expression, suggesting robust neuralization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Cyclopamine inhibits Isl1/2 and Nkx2.2 expression in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs with an IC50 around 25 nM.
claims.source: First, we treated nEBs with the Smo inhibitor cyclopamine (Cooper et al., 1998; Gaffield et al., 1999; Incardona et al., 2000a) and found that cyclopamine inhibited Isl1/2 and Nkx2.2 expression with an IC50 around 25 nM (Figure 1S).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1S.

claims.claim: ShhN induces the Hedgehog response in Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but not in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs.
claims.source: We found that ShhN (soluble N-terminal Shh) was able to induce the Hh response both in Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but not in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs, (Figure 1T)
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1T.

claims.claim: Ptch1-/- cells respond to Shh via Ptch2.
claims.source: corroborating our report that Ptch1-/- cells respond to Shh via Ptch2 (Alfaro et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claims.claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- fibroblasts co-transfected with Gli:Luciferase and Ptch1, then co-cultured with ShhN-transfected cells, activate the Hedgehog response.
claims.source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- fibroblasts co-transfected with Gli:Luciferase, a Hh pathway reporter (Taipale et al., 2000) and Ptch1, then co-cultured with ShhN-transfected cells, activate the Hh response (Figure 1U).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1U.

claims.claim: ShhN alone is unable to activate the Hedgehog pathway in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- cells.
claims.source: ShhN alone was unable to activate the Hh pathway in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- cells, consistent with results obtained with nEBs (Figure 1T).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1T.

claims.claim: The ability to respond to exogenous ShhN is lost in the absence of Ptch1/2, but can be restored with Ptch1 transfection.
claims.source: Thus, the ability to respond to exogenous ShhN is lost in the absence of Ptch1/2, but can be restored with Ptch1 transfection.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing restoration of Shh response upon Ptch1 transfection.

claims.claim: Mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells resembled Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs in their near complete absence of Nkx2.2+ cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of the two cell lines resembled Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs as judged by their near complete absence of Nkx2.2+ cells, and had fewer Olig2+ cells than expected for a 1:1 mosaic.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claims.claim: Mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells had fewer Olig2+ cells than expected for a 1:1 mosaic.
claims.source: Interestingly, mosaic nEBs comprised 1:1 of the two cell lines resembled Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs as judged by their near complete absence of Nkx2.2+ cells, and had fewer Olig2+ cells than expected for a 1:1 mosaic.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claims.claim: The reduced Nkx2.2+ and Olig2+ cells in mosaic nEBs is consistent with extracellular flux of Ptch1/2 substrates from Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: Because Shh is genetically absent from these nEBs and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- mESCs are ligand insensitive, we interpreted this result as consistent with extracellular flux of Ptch1/2 substrates from Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- mESCs in which Ptch1/2 are intact, and inconsistent with Shh sequestration from this compartment of cells.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claims.claim: Co-culture of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells with Smo-/- cells significantly decreased Nkx2.2+ cells and increased Olig2+ cells.
claims.source: In contrast, co-culture of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells with Smo-/- cells significantly decreased Nkx2.2+ cells and increased Olig2+ cells, rejecting the null hypothesis.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mosaic nEBs.

claims.claim: The changes in Nkx2.2+ and Olig2+ cells in mosaic nEBs represent a dorsal shift in the identity of the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cell compartment.
claims.source: We interpret this as a dorsal shift in the identity of the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cell compartment, as Nkx2.2 is a marker of a more ventral neural progenitor domain than Olig2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claims.claim: Ptch1:LacZ levels were low in Ptch1+/LacZ and Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but robust in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- nEBs at 72 hr.
claims.source: At 72 hr, Ptch1:LacZ levels were low in Ptch1+/LacZ and Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but robust in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/- nEBs (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Ptch1:LacZ levels were reduced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but remained elevated in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs.
claims.source: Ptch1:LacZ levels were reduced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- nEBs but remained elevated in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs had reduced Ptch:LacZ despite Ptch1/2 loss.
claims.source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Smo-/- Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs had reduced Ptch:LacZ despite Ptch1/2 loss.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Ptch1:LacZ is a reliable output for Hedgehog pathway activity across cell lines.
claims.source: These data suggest that Ptch1:LacZ is a reliable output for Hh pathway activity across cell lines.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between Ptch1:LacZ levels and neural progenitor markers.

claims.claim: Ptch1:LacZ was strongly induced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs after 72 hr differentiation.
claims.source: We found that Ptch1:LacZ was strongly induced in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs after 72 hr differentiation (Figure 3C), and this high level of expression persisted for several days.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Ptch1:LacZ expression is suppressed after treatment with cyclopamine, indicating that Ptch1:LacZ upregulation requires Smoothened.
claims.source: Ptch1:LacZ expression is suppressed after treatment with cyclopamine, indicating that Ptch1:LacZ upregulation requires Smo (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs have robust ventral neural progenitor identity.
claims.source: We observed robust ventral neural progenitor identity only in Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Disp1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- nEBs had widespread Pax7+ progenitors, indicating a low level of Hedgehog pathway activation.
claims.source: By contrast Disp1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- had widespread Pax7+ progenitors, indicating a low level of Hh pathway activation (Figure 3D–I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D-I.

claims.claim: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs mosaic 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells yielded Ptch1:LacZ signal closely reflecting the relative mESC contribution of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- nEBs mosaic 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells yielded Ptch1:LacZ signal closely reflecting the relative mESC contribution of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: When Disp1-/-;Shh-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1:LacZ levels in the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells significantly declined.
claims.source: However, when Disp1-/-;Shh-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1:LacZ levels in the Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells significantly declined (Figure 3J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claims.claim: Only small differences were found in Ptch1:LacZ signal derived from Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- mESCs co-cultured 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-, Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells.
claims.source: By contrast, only small differences were found in Ptch1:LacZ signal derived from Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- mESCs co-cultured 1:1 with Disp1-/-;Shh-/-, Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/- or Disp1-/-;Shh-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/- cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Smoothened is the target of the inhibitory cargo of Ptch1/2 activity.
claims.source: This supports the notion that Smo is the target of the inhibitory cargo of Ptch1/2 activity.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Smo-/- cells do not show changes in Ptch1:LacZ in mosaic nEBs.

claims.claim: Changes in LacZ levels in mosaic nEBs are not attributable to disparities in cell growth or adhesion during the culture period.
claims.source: Labeling the two cell compartments using Cell Tracker dyes, and assessing the resulting mosaic nEBs showed equivalent relative contributions after 48 hr (Figure 3K), indicating that changes in LacZ levels in mosaic nEBs are not attributable to disparities in cell growth or adhesion during the culture period.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3K.

claims.claim: Endogenous Ptch1/2 suppress the Hedgehog response non-cell autonomously in cells lacking Ptch1/2 activity.
claims.source: These results suggest that endogenous Ptch1/2 suppress the Hh response non-cell autonomously in cells lacking Ptch1/2 activity.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the mosaic nEB experiments.

claims.claim: Significantly less Ptch1:LacZ signal was obtained from nEBs containing Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells as compared with nEBs containing parental Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: Significantly less Ptch1:LacZ signal was obtained from nEBs containing Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells as compared with nEBs containing parental Shh-/- cells (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: nEBs are cultured in a cholesterol-free environment and likely upregulate cholesterol synthesis.
claims.source: Because nEBs are cultured in a cholesterol-free environment, they likely upregulate cholesterol synthesis (Brown and Goldstein, 1986).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from established knowledge about cholesterol regulation and citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Accumulation of 7DHC, or a 7DHC derivative, in Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells may provide a larger pool of the Ptch1/2 cargo, increasing secretion of the Smo-inhibitory sterol.
claims.source: Accumulation of 7DHC, or a 7DHC derivative (Bijlsma et al., 2006; Sever et al., 2016) in Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells may thus provide a larger pool of the Ptch1/2 cargo, increasing secretion of the Smo-inhibitory sterol, possibly 7DHC.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claims.claim: A decreased Hedgehog response was observed in nEBs treated with 7DHC compared to control treatment with cholesterol.
claims.source: Corroborating earlier findings (Bijlsma et al., 2006), we observed a decreased Hh response in nEBs treated with 7DHC compared to control treatment with cholesterol, regardless of whether the nEB was mosaic or comprised exclusively of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: A larger inhibition of the Hedgehog response by exogenous 7DHC was observed in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells co-cultured 1:1 in nEBs with Shh-/- as opposed to Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells.
claims.source: We additionally saw differences between the mosaic nEBs. A larger inhibition of the Hh response by exogenous 7DHC was observed in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells co-cultured 1:1 in nEBs with Shh-/- as opposed to Shh-/-;7dhcr-/- cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Cells containing Ptch1/2 may be able to process or transport exogenous 7DHC into a more potent non-cell autonomous inhibitor of the Hedgehog response in neighboring Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: We speculate that cells containing Ptch1/2 may be able to process or transport exogenous 7DHC into a more potent non-cell autonomous inhibitor of the Hh response in neighboring Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claims.claim: The findings are consistent with Ptch1/2 antiporter activity mediating secretion of 7DHC, or an oxysterol derivative like 3β,5α-dihydroxycholest-7-en-6-one, as a mechanism to inhibit Smoothened in neighboring cells.
claims.source: These findings are consistent with Ptch1/2 antiporter activity mediating secretion of 7DHC, or an oxysterol derivative like 3β,5α-dihydroxycholest-7-en-6-one (Sever et al., 2016), as a mechanism to inhibit Smo in neighboring cells.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data with citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Motor neurons arise from a population of neural progenitors in the ventral neural tube, and Hedgehog pathway activation is required for motor neuron differentiation in vivo as well as in nEBs.
claims.source: Motor neurons arise from a population of neural progenitors in the ventral neural tube, and Hh pathway activation is required for motor neuron differentiation in vivo as well as in nEBs.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about motor neuron development.

claims.claim: HB9:GFP+ cells had motor neuron morphology and co-labeled with Isl1/2 immunostain.
claims.source: HB9:GFP+ cells had motor neuron morphology and co-labeled with Isl1/2 immunostain, and thus serve as a measure for motor neuron induction (Figure 5B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: A small but significant increase in HB9:GFP+ motor neurons was observed when HB9:GFP cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells as compared to Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: We observed a small but significant increase in HB9:GFP+motor neurons when these cells were co-cultured with Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells as compared to Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells (Figure 5A,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,C.

claims.claim: 10 nM and 100 nM SAG induces motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells under all mosaic conditions.
claims.source: As predicted, 10 nM and 100 nM SAG induces motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells under all mosaic conditions (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: A strong synergistic effect was observed between Ptch1/2 loss in surrounding cells and SAG-induced motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells.
claims.source: However, a strong synergistic effect was observed between Ptch1/2 loss in surrounding cells and SAG-induced motor neuron differentiation in HB9:GFP cells (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: Compared to Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction at both SAG concentrations.
claims.source: We found that compared to Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction at both SAG concentrations
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction to an intermediate degree, presumably via Ptch2 activity.
claims.source: while Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells also suppressed motor neuron induction to an intermediate degree (presumably via Ptch2 activity).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data and inference about Ptch2 activity.

claims.claim: The observation of synergistic effects between Ptch1/2 loss and SAG is consistent with Ptch1/2 cargo acting as a SAG antagonist.
claims.source: This observation is consistent with Ptch1/2 cargo acting as a SAG antagonist and is not easily reconciled with impaired Hh ligand sequestration due to the lack of Ptch1/2 in the environment, as this scenario should have little effect on SAG-mediated Smo activation.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claims.claim: Three-part mosaic nEBs consisting of 94% Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells facilitated robust Shh-mediated HB9:GFP+ motor neuron induction.
claims.source: Three-part mosaic nEBs consisting of 94% Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/- or Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells facilitated robust Shh-mediated HB9:GFP+ motor neuron induction.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Negligible GFP expression was observed in mosaic nEBs principally comprised of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: In contrast, we observed negligible GFP expression in mosaic nEBs principally comprised of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells (Figure 6A,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A,D.

claims.claim: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were not observed when Shh overexpressing cells were omitted.
claims.source: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were not observed when Shh overexpressing cells were omitted.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: The response to Shh is strongly enhanced by Ptch1/2 absence in nearby cells.
claims.source: Thus, the response to Shh is strongly enhanced by Ptch1/2 absence in nearby cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced motor neuron induction.

claims.claim: No difference in extracellular Shh staining was found in various mosaic nEBs.
claims.source: We found no difference in extracellular Shh staining in various mosaic nEBs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), further supporting the idea that non-cell autonomous inhibition by Ptch1/2 of the Hh response does not involve Shh sequestration.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Shh robustly induced HB9:GFP+ motor neurons in nEBs consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: Shh robustly induced HB9:GFP+ motor neurons in nEBs consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Motor neuron induction was negligible in nEBs primarily consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Shh-/- cells.
claims.source: while motor neuron induction was negligible in nEBs primarily consisting of 94% Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/- and Disp1-/-;Shh-/- cells (Figure 6B,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,D.

claims.claim: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were induced efficiently only in predominantly Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs.
claims.source: HB9:GFP+ motor neurons were induced efficiently only in predominantly Ptch1-/-;Ptch2-/-;Smo-/- nEBs (Figure 6C,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claims.claim: In nEBs largely comprised of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, even a minor fraction of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction.
claims.source: In nEBs largely comprised of Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, even a minor fraction of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppressed motor neuron induction (Figure 6E,F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claims.claim: The properties of Ptch1/2 containing cells are dominant over those of cells lacking Ptch1/2 function.
claims.source: This indicates that the properties of Ptch1/2 containing cells are dominant over those of cells lacking Ptch1/2 function, further supporting the notion that Ptch1/2 function mediates the secretion of a Smo inhibitor that de-sensitizes cells to the effects of Shh.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing dominant inhibitory effects.

claims.claim: Ptch1/2 mediate the secretion of a Smoothened inhibitor that affects the Hedgehog response both cell autonomously and in nearby cells.
claims.source: A logical interpretation of these results is that Ptch1/2 mediate the secretion of a Smo inhibitor that affects the Hh response both cell autonomously, and in nearby cells.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from all the experimental data.

claims.claim: Observations similar to the current study but using overexpressed Ptch1 have been reported in fibroblasts.
claims.source: Observations similar to ours but using overexpressed Ptch1 have been reported in fibroblasts and our experiments support this finding (Bijlsma et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Detecting non-cell autonomous activities of Ptch1/2 expressed at endogenous levels in nEBs resolves the argument that overexpressed Ptch1/2 constructs could have non-physiological effects.
claims.source: Detecting these activities of Ptch1/2 expressed at endogenous levels in nEBs resolves the argument that overexpressed Ptch1/2 constructs could have non-physiological effects.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the significance of the current findings.

claims.claim: Cells with a dorsal identity (Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/-) are better non-cell autonomous repressors of the Hedgehog response than cells with a more ventral identity (Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/-).
claims.source: Notably, cells with a dorsal identity (Disp1-/-;Ptch1-/-;Shh-/-) are better non-cell autonomous repressors of the Hh response than cells with a more ventral identity (Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Shh-/-).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data.

claims.claim: The variation in non-cell autonomous repression by Ptch1-/- lines is speculated to be due to varying levels of Ptch2 activity.
claims.source: We speculate that this is due to varying levels of Ptch2 activity.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed variation.

claims.claim: The loss of Smoothened decreases the ability of Ptch1/2 to inhibit the Hedgehog response non-cell autonomously.
claims.source: It also appears that the loss of Smo decreases the ability of Ptch1/2 to inhibit the Hh response non-cell autonomously.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data.

claims.claim: The decrease in non-cell autonomous inhibition by Ptch1/2 upon Smoothened loss is easily explained by a decrease in Ptch1/2 levels as Ptch1/2 expression is under the control of Smoothened.
claims.source: This observation is easily explained by a decrease in Ptch1/2 levels as Ptch1/2 expression is under the control of Smo.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on established knowledge of Hh pathway regulation.

claims.claim: Even in the complete absence of Hedgehog pathway activation, Ptch1/2 can still inhibit Smoothened.
claims.source: Thus, even in the complete absence of Hh pathway activation, Ptch1/2 can still inhibit Smo.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ptch1/2 inhibit Smo in Smo-/- cells.

claims.claim: In tissues without detectable levels of Ptch1/2, Smoothened remains inactive.
claims.source: This is consistent with the observation that in tissues without detectable levels of Ptch1/2, Smo remains inactive.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about Smo regulation.

claims.claim: Ptch1 localizes to late endosomes while mediating Shh uptake.
claims.source: We previously demonstrated that Ptch1 localizes to late endosomes while mediating Shh uptake, and that Shh signaling requires endosomal acidification (Incardona et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claims.claim: Shh signaling requires endosomal acidification.
claims.source: We previously demonstrated that Ptch1 localizes to late endosomes while mediating Shh uptake, and that Shh signaling requires endosomal acidification (Incardona et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claims.claim: Conserved acidic residues required for proton flux in prokaryotic RNDs are also required for Ptch1 to repress Smoothened.
claims.source: Conserved acidic residues required for proton flux in prokaryotic RNDs are also required for Ptch1 to repress Smo (Alfaro et al., 2014; Strutt et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Ptch1/2 may enrich the endosomal lumen or intraluminal vesicular in multivesicular endosomes (MVEs) with a Smoothened inhibitor.
claims.source: One possibility is that Ptch1/2 enrich the endosomal lumen or intraluminal vesicular in multivesicular endosomes (MVEs) with a Smo inhibitor.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claims.claim: Exosomal release would allow the Smoothened inhibitor to enter the extracellular environment and regulate Smoothened both cell autonomously as well as non-cell autonomously.
claims.source: Exosomal release would allow this inhibitor to enter the extracellular environment and regulate Smo both cell autonomously as well as non-cell autonomously.

results.result: The authors characterize neural differentiation patterns in a panel of genome-edited mESC lines with various combinations of Ptch1, Ptch2, Shh, and Smo mutations. Each cell line differentiates into neural progenitor identities consistent with established Hedgehog signaling models, with ventral markers (Nkx2.2, Olig2, Isl1/2) indicating high pathway activity and dorsal markers (Pax7) indicating pathway inactivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C45 collectively demonstrate that the genome-edited cell lines behave as predicted by canonical Hh signaling models. The immunostaining data (Figure 1) shows appropriate neural progenitor marker expression patterns across all genotypes, with Smo invariably required for pathway activation and Ptch1/2 acting as negative regulators. This validation is essential for subsequent mosaic experiments.

results.result: The authors validate that Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells have constitutive, Shh-independent Hedgehog pathway activation that is Smoothened-dependent. Cyclopamine inhibits the response with IC50 ~25 nM, ShhN cannot activate the pathway in these cells, but Ptch1 transfection restores Shh responsiveness.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C51 are well-supported by experimental data (Figures 1S, 1T, 1U). The cyclopamine dose-response, lack of ShhN response, and rescue by Ptch1 transfection collectively validate that these cells are appropriate for assessing non-cell autonomous Ptch1/2 effects. The IC50 determination and rescue experiments provide strong mechanistic evidence.

results.result: In mosaic nEBs composed 1:1 of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- and Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells, the authors observe fewer Nkx2.2+ and Olig2+ cells than expected, suggesting non-cell autonomous inhibition of the Hedgehog response by Ptch1/2-expressing cells. Co-culture with Smo-/- cells produces a dorsal shift in Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cell identity.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C56 provide the first direct evidence for non-cell autonomous Ptch1/2 activity. The mosaic nEB data (Figure 2) shows deviation from the null hypothesis of purely cell-autonomous regulation. The interpretation that this reflects extracellular flux of Ptch1/2 substrates is reasonable given the genetic absence of Shh and ligand insensitivity of the reporter cells.

results.result: The authors establish Ptch1:LacZ as a reliable, lineage-restricted reporter of Hedgehog pathway activity across their cell line panel. Ptch1:LacZ levels correlate with neural progenitor marker expression, are maximal at 72 hr differentiation, and require Smoothened activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C62 are well-supported by experimental data (Figure 3A-C). The correlation between Ptch1:LacZ levels and ventral neural progenitor markers, time-course data, and cyclopamine sensitivity validate this reporter for subsequent mosaic experiments. This provides a quantitative, high-throughput alternative to immunostaining.

results.result: Using Disp1-/- cell lines to eliminate all Hedgehog ligand signaling, the authors demonstrate that Ptch1/2-expressing cells non-cell autonomously suppress Ptch1:LacZ expression in neighboring Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells. This effect requires Smoothened in the responding cells and is not due to differential cell growth.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C70 provide strong evidence for non-cell autonomous Ptch1/2 activity independent of ligand sequestration. The use of Disp1-/- cells eliminates paracrine Hedgehog signaling, and the Smo-dependence of the effect (C67-C68) supports Smo as the target. Cell tracker experiments (C69) rule out differential proliferation as a confound. This is a key result supporting the antiporter model.

results.result: Loss of 7dhcr enhances the ability of cells to non-cell autonomously inhibit the Hedgehog response in neighboring Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- cells. Exogenous 7DHC inhibits the Hedgehog response, with greater inhibition when Ptch1/2-expressing cells are present, supporting 7DHC or its derivatives as candidate Ptch1/2 cargo molecules.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C77 are supported by experimental data (Figure 4). The enhanced non-cell autonomous inhibition by 7dhcr-/- cells (C71) and differential effects of exogenous 7DHC in mosaic vs. monotypic cultures (C74-C75) provide evidence for sterol involvement. However, the interpretation remains somewhat speculative (C73, C76) as the exact molecular species is not identified. The results are consistent with but do not definitively prove the model.

results.result: Using HB9:GFP motor neuron differentiation as a readout, the authors show that Ptch1/2 in surrounding cells suppress motor neuron induction in wild-type cells. SAG-induced motor neuron differentiation shows strong synergy with Ptch1/2 loss in surrounding cells, consistent with Ptch1/2 cargo acting as a SAG antagonist rather than through ligand sequestration.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C85 are well-supported by experimental data (Figure 5). The synergistic effect between SAG and Ptch1/2 loss (C82) is particularly important as it argues against ligand sequestration and supports a direct Smo-inhibitory mechanism. The dose-dependent effects and intermediate phenotype of Ptch1LacZ/-;Shh-/- cells (C84) suggest Ptch2 compensation, consistent with other results.

results.result: In three-part mosaic nEBs with sparse Shh-expressing cells, the authors demonstrate that Ptch1/2 absence in the majority cell population strongly enhances Shh-mediated motor neuron induction in HB9:GFP reporter cells. Extracellular Shh levels are unchanged across conditions, arguing against ligand sequestration as the mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C93 are strongly supported by experimental data (Figure 6A-D, Figure 6—supplement 1). The dramatic differences in motor neuron induction based on Ptch1/2 status of surrounding cells (C86-C87, C91-C92), combined with equivalent extracellular Shh staining (C90), provide compelling evidence that non-cell autonomous effects are mediated by secreted inhibitor rather than ligand sequestration. The Smo-dependence (C93) further supports this model.

results.result: In four-part mosaic nEBs, even a minor fraction of Ptch1+/LacZ;Shh-/- cells suppresses Shh-mediated motor neuron induction in a predominantly Ptch1LacZ/LacZ;Ptch2-/-;Shh-/- environment, demonstrating that Ptch1/2-containing cells have dominant inhibitory properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C95 are supported by experimental data (Figure 6E-F). The dominant inhibitory effect of even small numbers of Ptch1/2-expressing cells strongly supports secretion of a diffusible inhibitor rather than a cell-autonomous or activating mechanism. This is a key result distinguishing between alternative models.

results.result: The authors conclude that Ptch1/2 mediate secretion of a Smoothened inhibitor that affects the Hedgehog response both cell autonomously and non-cell autonomously. This extends prior observations using overexpressed Ptch1 by demonstrating the effect with endogenous Ptch1/2 levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C98 represent the main conclusion, which is well-supported by the collective experimental evidence from mosaic nEBs. The use of endogenous expression levels (C98) addresses a key limitation of prior work (C97). However, the exact molecular identity of the secreted inhibitor remains unidentified, which is a limitation.

results.result: The authors observe that different Ptch1-/- cell lines vary in their non-cell autonomous inhibitory activity, with dorsal cells being more effective inhibitors than ventral cells. They speculate this reflects varying Ptch2 levels. Loss of Smoothened decreases non-cell autonomous inhibition, likely due to reduced Ptch1/2 expression, but Ptch1/2 can still inhibit Smo even without pathway activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C104 are supported by experimental observations, though the interpretation regarding Ptch2 levels (C100) is speculative. The observation that Smo loss reduces non-cell autonomous inhibition (C101-C102) is consistent with feedback regulation of Ptch1/2 expression. The conclusion that Ptch1/2 can inhibit Smo without pathway activation (C103) is well-supported.

results.result: The authors propose a mechanistic model in which Ptch1/2 function as proton-driven antiporters in acidified endosomal compartments, enriching endosomal lumen or multivesicular endosomes with a Smoothened inhibitor that is released via exosomes to regulate Smo both cell autonomously and non-cell autonomously.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C107 cite prior work establishing Ptch1 localization to late endosomes and requirement for acidification and conserved acidic residues. However, claims C108-C109 are speculative models not directly tested in this study. While consistent with the data, alternative mechanisms for secretion are not ruled out. Additional experiments would be needed to validate this specific model.

results.result: The authors conclude that cells enriched in sterol precursors (7dhcr-/-) are more effective non-cell autonomous inhibitors, and that 7DHC becomes more potent when acted upon by Ptch1/2 activity, suggesting the Ptch1/2 cargo becomes inhibitory after translocation or secretion.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C111 are well-supported by the 7dhcr experiments (Figure 4). Claims C112-C113 represent reasonable inferences from the data showing enhanced inhibition in mosaic cultures with Ptch1/2-expressing cells. However, the exact molecular species and mechanism of activation remain speculative. The conclusion is consistent with but not definitively proven by the data.

results.result: The authors discuss implications for cancer biology, noting that Ptch1/2 disruption in tumors may enhance Smoothened activation in adjacent stromal cells non-cell autonomously, but that cells remain sensitive to Hedgehog ligands even without Ptch1/2, suggesting ligand-targeting therapies remain viable.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C117 represent reasonable implications of the findings for cancer therapy, supported by citations to prior literature on stromal cell responses to Shh-expressing tumors (C115). The prediction that ligand-targeting strategies remain viable (C116-C117) follows logically from the demonstration that Ptch1/2-null cells respond to Shh when Ptch1 is restored.

results.result: The authors propose that Ptch1/2 act broadly and communally to inhibit Smoothened in tissues undergoing patterning, with non-cell autonomous inhibition mediated by antiporter activity rather than ligand sequestration. This model suggests local Shh sensitivity is highly buffered and equalized between cells, aiding formation of smooth response gradients.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C121 are well-supported by the experimental data showing non-cell autonomous inhibition in Shh-/- nEBs and dominant effects of small numbers of Ptch1/2-expressing cells. Claims C122-C123 represent a broader model for morphogen gradient formation that is consistent with the findings but extends beyond what is directly demonstrated. The model is plausible but would require additional in vivo validation.

results.result: The introduction establishes the biological importance of Hedgehog signaling, the molecular identities of key pathway components (Smoothened as a GPCR, Patched as an RND family antiporter), the prevailing model of Ptch-mediated Smo inhibition, and multiple lines of evidence suggesting the endogenous Ptch cargo is a steroidal molecule, though no Smo-regulatory Ptch substrate has been definitively identified.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C34 represent established knowledge and prior work that provides context for the current study. These are well-supported by appropriate citations to the literature. The summary of evidence for a steroidal cargo (C17-C27) is comprehensive and accurately represents the state of the field. This background appropriately motivates the experimental approach.
